name: BlackRock

summary.text: BlackRock is an asset manager founded in 1988 by Larry Fink, Rob Kapito, Sue Wagner, Barbara Novick, Ben Golub, Hugh Frater, Ralph Schlosstein and Keith Anderson. During the 2008 financial crisis, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York retained BlackRock Financial Management as investment manager for the Maiden Lane LLC vehicles, which held assets acquired in the Bear Stearns and AIG rescues.

sources.title: BlackRock history

sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
sources.title: Maiden Lane Transactions

facts.claim: In 2008 the Federal Reserve Bank of New York retained BlackRock Financial Management as investment manager for Maiden Lane LLC (about $30 billion of Bear Stearns assets), Maiden Lane II LLC ($20.5 billion of AIG residential mortgage-backed securities) and Maiden Lane III LLC ($29.3 billion of CDOs bought from AIG Financial Products counterparties).

sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
sources.title: Maiden Lane Transactions

facts.claim: BlackRock developed and sells Aladdin, an investment and risk-management technology platform used by institutions including asset managers, banks, insurers and pension funds.

sources.title: Aladdin by BlackRock

facts.claim: BlackRock Financial Management was hired in March 2008 to manage the Maiden Lane LLC portfolio of former Bear Stearns assets valued at $30 billion as of March 14, 2008 and pledged as security for $29 billion in New York Fed financing. On April 7, 2008 House Oversight Chairman Henry Waxman wrote to New York Fed President Timothy Geithner questioning the award of this potentially lucrative position to BlackRock without competition; he said he did not dispute the need for quick action but noted that emergency no-bid contracts typically have a short duration and are replaced with long-term contracts through full and open competition, and asked whether the Fed could later solicit competing bids.
facts.quote: BlackRock Financial Management was hired to manage the portfolio. / the award of this potentially lucrative position to BlackRock without competition / emergency no-bid contracts have a short duration and are replaced with long-term contracts through full and open competition

sources.publisher: U.S. House of Representatives (Office of Speaker Emerita Pelosi, archived release)
sources.title: Chairman Waxman Requests Details of Federal Reserve's No-Bid Arrangement with BlackRock

facts.claim: American Banker reported on July 15, 2009, citing contract terms released by the New York Fed, that BlackRock would get at least $71 million in the first year of its contracts to oversee the Maiden Lane assets: $45.3 million for the Maiden Lane holdings taken over from Bear Stearns and $25.5 million for the Maiden Lane II and Maiden Lane III investments bought from AIG, with the agreements set to run at least three years, asset-based fees that shrink as the portfolios decrease, and the potential for an additional $50 million or more.
facts.quote: BlackRock is set to receive $45.3 million this year for running the Maiden Lane holdings that the Federal Reserve took over from Bear Stearns, based on contract terms released by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. The company will get $25.5 million to manage the Maiden Lane II and the Maiden Lane III investments that the Fed purchased from AIG.

sources.title: BlackRock to Get $71M on Maiden Lane

facts.claim: GAO's July 2011 audit of the Federal Reserve's emergency assistance (GAO-11-696), which covered the Maiden Lane vehicles, found that the Reserve Banks, mainly the New York Fed, awarded 103 contracts worth $659.4 million from 2008 through 2010 to support emergency work, that a few contracts accounted for most vendor spending, and that the Reserve Banks relied more extensively on vendors for programs that assisted a single institution than for broad-based programs. (GAO finding.)
facts.quote: The Reserve Banks relied more extensively on vendors for programs that assisted a single institution than for broad-based programs

facts.claim: GAO-11-696 found that the New York Fed took steps to manage conflicts of interest for its employees, directors and program vendors, but that opportunities exist to strengthen its conflict policies. A related GAO testimony table lists 42 contracts for Maiden Lane (Bear Stearns) totaling $158.4 million and 36 subvendors paid $3.3 million across the three Maiden Lane programs, CPFF and TALF. (GAO finding.)
facts.quote: the New York Fed took steps to manage conflicts of interest for its employees, directors, and program vendors, but opportunities exist to strengthen its conflict policies

facts.claim: On June 12, 2009 Barclays announced a binding offer from BlackRock for Barclays Global Investors (including iShares) for approximately US$13.5 billion: US$6.6 billion in cash and about US$6.9 billion in 37.784 million new BlackRock shares at the June 11, 2009 closing price, giving Barclays an economic interest of about 19.9% of the enlarged BlackRock; the 19.9% was to consist of 4.9% of common stock with the balance in Series B Participating Preferred Stock, and Barclays was to take two board seats. The combined firm was to be named BlackRock Global Investors.
facts.quote: The consideration would be approximately US$13.5 billion (£8.2 billion) of which US$6.6 billion (£4.0 billion) would be received in cash and approximately US$6.9 billion (£4.2 billion) in shares based on the closing price of BlackRock's common stock on 11 June 2009. / The proposed economic interest of approximately 19.9% to be held by Barclays would consist of 4.9% of the enlarged common stock of BlackRock outstanding after the transaction, with the balance being satisfied by the issue of Series B Participating Preferred Stock.

sources.title: Barclays PLC Form 6-K: binding offer from BlackRock for Barclays Global Investors
BlackRock press release on the agreement to acquire Barclays Global Investors

facts.claim: BlackRock completed the BGI acquisition on December 1, 2009. Its Form 8-K reports cash consideration of about $6.65 billion plus 3,031,516 common shares, 26,888,001 Series B preferred shares and 7,647,254 Series D preferred shares; an 8-K/A values the 37,566,771-share stock component at about $8.53 billion at closing. Barclays reported the consideration at completion as US$15.2 billion, including 37.567 million new BlackRock shares giving it a 19.9% economic interest. In May 2012 Barclays moved to sell its entire holding, with BlackRock repurchasing up to $1.0 billion of its stock.
facts.quote: The consideration at completion was US$15.2 billion (£9.5 billion), including 37.567 million new BlackRock shares giving Barclays an economic interest of 19.9% of the enlarged BlackRock group.

facts.quote: BlackRock, Inc. is one of the largest publicly traded investment management firms in the United States with $1.307 trillion of assets under management at December 31, 2008. / At December 31, 2009, BlackRock managed $3.346 trillion of AUM, a 156%, or $2.039 trillion, increase relative to BlackRock's reported AUM at December 31, 2008.

facts.claim: On March 24, 2020, the day after the Secondary Market Corporate Credit Facility was announced, the New York Fed retained BlackRock Financial Markets Advisory as a third-party vendor to serve as the facility's investment manager, citing BlackRock's experience buying large volumes of corporate debt in the secondary market, its knowledge of corporate debt markets, and its operational and technology capabilities.
facts.quote: retained BlackRock Financial Markets Advisory as a third-party vendor

sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
sources.title: Secondary Market Corporate Credit Facility

facts.claim: Bloomberg reported in May 2020 that under its 66-page contract with the New York Fed for the corporate credit facilities, BlackRock would receive no trading commissions but an administration fee starting at $2 million for the second quarter of 2020 and declining to $750,000 by the fourth quarter, plus a sliding-scale rate on non-ETF corporate debt (2.5 basis points on the first $10 billion, stepping down toward 50 cents per $10,000 as assets approached $350 billion), and could collect no fees on any ETFs in the portfolio; Bloomberg estimated the firm could earn as much as $40 million a year.
facts.quote: According to BlackRock's 66-page contract with the New York Fed, the firm will receive no commissions for executing trades. Instead, it will take an administration fee that starts at $2 million for the second quarter this year and declines to $750,000 by the fourth quarter. / BlackRock's management agreement with the Federal Reserve Bank of New York bars the firm, the world's largest issuer of exchange-traded funds, from collecting fees on any ETFs in the portfolio it assembles.

sources.title: BlackRock's Role as Fed Adviser Confers More 'Clout' Than Fees

facts.claim: On March 24, 2008 the New York Fed published a summary of terms for its financing of JPMorgan Chase's acquisition of Bear Stearns, stating that BlackRock Financial Management had been retained by the New York Fed to manage and liquidate the assets. The terms described a $29 billion New York Fed loan backed by a $30 billion portfolio of Bear Stearns assets valued as of March 14, 2008, and a $1 billion subordinated note from JPMorgan Chase absorbing the first losses, both lent to a Delaware limited liability company with 10-year terms renewable by the New York Fed; the Fed loan carried the primary credit rate (then 2.5 percent) and the JPMorgan note that rate plus 450 basis points.

sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
sources.title: Press release of March 24, 2008: terms and conditions of the New York Fed financing in the JPMorgan Chase acquisition of Bear Stearns

facts.claim: The New York Fed's vendor information archive lists BlackRock Financial Management, Inc. as providing investment management and advisory services for Maiden Lane LLC, Maiden Lane II LLC and Maiden Lane III LLC, and records an October 15, 2010 update to the investment management agreements with BlackRock. The amended and restated agreement for Maiden Lane LLC, dated June 24, 2010, among the New York Fed, BlackRock and Maiden Lane LLC, provides that the manager is compensated under a fee schedule at Exhibit B, with certain costs billed separately, including residential portfolio reporting and document-related fees and transaction execution expenses such as broker fees and commissions.
facts.quote: Investment management and advisory services for ML LLC, ML II & ML III / For services hereunder, the Manager shall be compensated in accordance with Exhibit B attached hereto.

facts.claim: The Maiden Lane vehicles' audited financial statements report investment-manager fees within a single 'professional fees' line, described in the notes as primarily the fees of the investment manager, administrator and auditors plus loan servicing and disposition costs. Maiden Lane LLC's professional fees and other expenses were $68.6 million in 2010, $42.9 million in 2011, $12.1 million in 2012 and $6.0 million in 2013; Maiden Lane III LLC's professional fees were $9.0 million in 2008, $26.9 million in 2009, $19.8 million in 2011 and $10.8 million in 2012; Maiden Lane II LLC's were $10.2 million in 2010 and $7.9 million in 2011. The BlackRock-only amount is not broken out.
facts.quote: Professional fees and other expenses are primarily comprised of the fees charged by the Investment Manager, administrator, and independent auditors as well as fees and expenses related to the servicing and disposition of residential and commercial loans held by the Grantor Trusts

facts.claim: GAO-11-696 (July 2011) found that most of the Reserve Banks' emergency-program contracts, including 8 of the 10 highest-value contracts, were awarded noncompetitively, primarily due to exigent circumstances, and that these awards were consistent with the New York Fed's acquisition policies but the policies could be improved by additional guidance on the use of competition exceptions, such as seeking as much competition as practicable and limiting noncompetitive contracts to the exigency period. GAO recommended revising the acquisition policies so that Reserve Banks do not miss opportunities to obtain competition and receive the most favorable terms for services acquired. (GAO finding.)
facts.quote: most of the contracts, including 8 of the 10 highest-value contracts, were awarded noncompetitively, primarily due to exigent circumstances / These contract awards were consistent with FRBNY's acquisition policies, but the policies could be improved by providing additional guidance on the use of competition exceptions / to better ensure that Reserve Banks do not miss opportunities to obtain competition and receive the most favorable terms for services acquired

sources.title: GAO-11-696 Highlights: Federal Reserve System: Opportunities Exist to Strengthen Policies and Processes for Managing Emergency Assistance
GAO-11-696 (full report)

facts.claim: On vendor conflicts of interest, GAO-11-696 found that the New York Fed's onsite reviews of vendor compliance in some instances occurred as far as 12 months into a contract, that it had implemented a new vendor management policy but had not finalized another policy with comprehensive guidance on vendor conflict issues, and that new roles taken on by the New York Fed and its employees during the crisis created potential conflicts its Code of Conduct and other policies did not specifically address. GAO recommended that the New York Fed finalize the vendor conflict policy; it made seven recommendations in all, and the Board agreed they would benefit its response to future crises. (GAO finding.)
facts.quote: FRBNY's onsite reviews of vendor compliance in some instances occurred as far as 12 months into a contract. FRBNY implemented a new vendor management policy but has not yet finalized another new policy with comprehensive guidance on vendor conflict issues. / to reduce the risk that vendors may not be required to take steps to fully identify and mitigate all conflicts / New roles that FRBNY and its employees took on during the crisis created potential conflicts that the Code of Conduct and other FRBNY policies did not specifically address

(GAO finding.)

facts.claim: BlackRock's own annual reports give the scale of its Aladdin platform: the Form 10-K for 2009 states that over $9.0 trillion of positions were processed on the Aladdin operating platform; the Form 10-K for 2010 states that over $10 trillion of positions ran through the platform; and the Form 10-K for 2012 reports about $13.7 trillion of positions processed on Aladdin at year-end, 51 Aladdin clients and $14 trillion of assets on the platform. Later 10-Ks (2019 through 2023) describe Aladdin as an end-to-end software-as-a-service solution for investment and risk management, with technology services revenue of $1.3 billion in 2021, without giving a platform-wide asset total.
facts.quote: Over $9.0 trillion of positions are processed on our Aladdin operating platform

In a 2017 Bloomberg interview, Larry Fink said he hoped Aladdin would become the 'Android of finance'.

openQuestions: Brief claim 'BlackRock leveraged this insider visibility across every Wall Street balance sheet to purchase BGI' is not stated by any source found. What sources say: Waxman (April 2008) objected to the award 'without competition'; GAO-11-696 found the New York Fed 'took steps to manage conflicts of interest for its employees, directors, and program vendors, but opportunities exist to strengthen its conflict policies', that 8 of the 10 highest-value contracts were awarded noncompetitively 'primarily due to exigent circumstances', and that a comprehensive vendor-conflict policy had not been finalized; Bloomberg (May 2020) reported that the Fed assignment 'confers other benefits, including the U.S. government's endorsement of BlackRock as its go-to adviser'. No source links Maiden Lane information to the BGI purchase. GAO's BlackRock-specific vendor-selection and information-barrier passages were still not surfaced by three further searches of gao.gov; the full GAO-11-696 PDF must be read for them.

Brief claim that the Fed and Treasury 'lacked the technical infrastructure to model or value' the derivatives is not stated by any source found. Waxman wrote that he 'did not dispute the need for quick action'; GAO found the Reserve Banks 'relied more extensively on vendors for programs that assisted a single institution'; the New York Fed's 2020 SMCCF notice cited BlackRock's 'operational and technology capabilities'. None says the Fed could not value the assets.

Brief claim that bailout money 'permanently capitalized BlackRock' is not stated by any source. The reported Maiden Lane fees (at least $71 million in year one; up to roughly $50 million more over at least three years, per American Banker) are small next to the BGI price ($6.6 billion cash plus shares; US$15.2 billion at completion). Search results referred to BlackRock seeking a further $2.8 billion from equity investors and to 2009 Form 424B5 offerings, but no passage tying the BGI financing to its sources was retrieved; the owner may check BlackRock's December 2009 424B5 filings.

Brief claim 'pennies on the dollar' for BGI: no source characterizes the price. The sourced figures are a $13.5 billion offer (US$15.2 billion at completion) for a business that added $1.850 trillion of AUM, and Barclays recorded a gain that raised its Core Tier 1 ratio by an estimated 150-185 basis points.

Brief claim '$10T+ AUM' is supported and exceeded by BlackRock's 10-Ks: $11.6 trillion at end-2024 and $14.0 trillion at end-2025. The brief's description of BlackRock as an 'unelected clearinghouse for sovereign debt and corporate governance' is characterization, not a sourced fact, and is not recorded.

Aladdin scale: BlackRock's own 10-Ks now supply figures through 2012 ($9.0 trillion of positions, FY2009; over $10 trillion, FY2010; about $13.7 trillion of positions and $14 trillion of assets on the platform with 51 clients, FY2012), recorded as a documented fact; excerpts of the FY2019-FY2023 10-Ks give no platform-wide total. The $21.6 trillion (2020) figure remains sourced only to Wikipedia citing the FT; ft.com and vanityfair.com block the search crawler, and Bloomberg's 2017-2018 pieces give client-asset figures rather than a platform total. Replace the Wikipedia item with the 10-K item before approval, or leave the 2020 figure out.

Attribution check: the 'Series B Participating Preferred Stock / 4.9% of common stock' sentence appeared in the search results on the BGI deal alongside the Barclays June 12, 2009 6-K and BlackRock's Exhibit 99.1 press release; both are cited. Confirm which document holds it.

GAO-12-122T is cited for the '42 contracts for Maiden Lane (Bear Stearns) totaling $158.4 million' table; the date 2011-10-04 is the testimony's House hearing date as given in the search context and should be verified.

ProPublica's 2009 article 'Bailout Player BlackRock Becomes Biggest Money Manager' appeared in results but no passage was retrieved; it may be a useful reported source on the Maiden Lane-BGI timeline.

The March 24, 2008 terms were attributed by the search result to the New York Fed page rp080324b; a companion page, https://www.newyorkfed.org/newsevents/news/markets/2008/rp080324 , also exists and may be the press release proper. Confirm which page holds the sentence retaining BlackRock Financial Management.

The professional-fee figures were read from search extracts of the year-labelled Maiden Lane financial statements; the mapping of each figure to the cited statement should be confirmed on review, and the quoted note on what the line comprises was attributed to a later Maiden Lane LLC statement without the extract saying which year. The BlackRock-only fee is not broken out in any statement retrieved, and Exhibit B of the June 24, 2010 agreement (the fee schedule) was not retrieved; the fee rates remain known only from American Banker's July 2009 report.

GAO attribution: the line that BlackRock projected full repayment of the Maiden Lane II and III loans under stress scenarios was described in the search result as from GAO's 2011 AIG review; GAO-11-616 is cited for it but it may instead sit in GAO-11-716. Check which report holds it.

Founding inside Blackstone: Blackstone's S-1/A appears in the results in three amendments (also https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001393818/000104746907005078/a2178442zs-1a.htm and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001393818/000104746907005026/a2178442zs-1a.htm ); the first is cited and the passage should be confirmed in it. Encyclopedia.com reproduces a company-history reference work and is cited only for the July 1992 renaming and the 1995 PNC acquisition. The '$5 million credit line' from Blackstone appears only in tertiary profiles and is not recorded; sources differ on whether the separation dates to 1992 (management buyout) or 1994 (Blackstone's sale of its remaining interest).
